page: Vultr vx1-g-8c-32g is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is network-based, configured with a 1 GB capacity, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no dedicated GPUs bundled with this server configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates exceptional single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression rates all ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-core and multi-threaded workloads, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and software compilation via Clang, fall into the average tier (middle 50%). Memory bandwidth tests, PassMark database operations, and Redis SET operations also register average performance. For machine learning tasks, text generation using a small 135M parameter model is strong (top 25%), while prompt processing on a medium 7B model is weak (bottom 25%).

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC processor allocation and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server offers steady resource density for general-purpose workloads without the performance degradation associated with shared-core environments. The lack of large local storage means it relies on network-attached storage for data-heavy operations. It is well-suited for web serving, text processing, single-threaded data compression, lightweight database operations, and general-purpose application hosting.
description: Vultr vx1-g-8c-32g is a general-purpose virtual server from the VX1 Cloud Compute family, powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 32.0 GB of RAM, and 1 GB of network-based storage. The server excels in single-core tasks, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression benchmarks ranking in the top 10%. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations align with average tier expectations. Lacking a local GPU and featuring minimal default network storage, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources without massive local storage needs. It is highly suitable for web serving, text processing, software compilation, and general-purpose application hosting.
